newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank set to appoint Haferkamp to board.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank set to appoint Haferkamp to board.

text.p: The Bundesbank looks set to appoint Dieter Haferkamp to its board after the central bank said its central council had discussed Haferkamp's appointment on Thursday and made a recommendation to the Bonn government.

A spokesman for the bank said the government, which makes appointments to the Bundesbank board, had listened to the central bank's recommendation. But the spokesman declined to comment on whether the bank had recommended Haferkamp or not.

German newsletter Platow Brief reported on Friday that the government had appointed 59 year-old Haferkamp, who is head of the Bundesbank's personnel department. Government comment was not immediately available.
Media reports have speculated that Haferkamp would be named as the successor to Gerd Haeusler, who has left the Bundesbank to join Dresdner Bank AG.

Traditionally the government recommends Bundesbank board candidates to the Chancellor, who then officially appoints them for a term of eight years. The central bank itself is asked for comment but has no right to veto a candidate.
A newspaper reported in August that Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer had persuaded Chancellor Helmut Kohl to give the job to a Bundesbank man rather than make a political appointment.

The eighth seat on the Bundesbank's directorate, or board, has been vacant since Haeusler resigned earlier this year. Haeusler will start work on the management board of Dresdner, Germany's second largest commercial bank, in December.
